decision: WF-092 domain package and branch engine ownership

state.goal: Chain sequential multi-level approvals through a workflow: a branch engine reads quote properties, pushes an approval step (approver list + priority) onto each qualifying quote, runs the chain sequentially, and the last decision writes APPROVED or REJECTED.

measured_evidence.backend/dsr/crm_workflows: Exists. WF-030. Contact-based CRM workflow criteria and actions, keyed on activity families. It has no notion of an approval step, a priority rank, or a chained approver decision. Its collections are play-independent: crm_workflow, crm_workflow_run, crm_workflow_enrollment.
measured_evidence.backend/dsr/plays: Exists. WF-028. A Play is a one-off action fired by a signal. No approval step, no priority.
measured_evidence.backend/dsr/quoting_proposals: Exists. WF-093 and WF-098 quote rules. Owns quote vocabulary (QUOTES = wf086_quote, LINE_ITEMS = wf086_line_item) read as data. It does not model approvers.
measured_evidence.issue_instruction: backend/dsr/quote_approvals/ is the named domain package and is absent on main. The issue also says a package for the domain already exists must be extended instead.
measured_evidence.existing_approval_surface: backend/dsr/booking_approval.py exists and is single level, for meeting booking. It has no priority rank.

constraints: Must not edit any shared host file.
Domain module imports nothing but the store.
One approval workflow only. The spec says you cannot duplicate it.
Cap of five sequences and ten approvers per sequence must be enforced.
Sequential, All and Any approver requirements must all exist.
A quote that matched a branch but has no approval step must auto-approve.

domain_package.instructions: Which Python package should own the WF-092 domain rules?

criteria.new_quote_approvals: Create backend/dsr/quote_approvals/ as the issue names. It owns the branch predicate, the priority ordering, the chain state machine, its vocabulary, its errors and its inferences.
criteria.extend_quoting_proposals: Add the approval modules to the existing backend/dsr/quoting_proposals/ package instead of creating a second package for the same quoting domain.

branch_engine.instructions: Should this feature reuse an existing engine, or own its own branch engine?

criteria.own_branch_engine: Build a small branch engine inside quote_approvals. It evaluates the researched branch conditions against a quote record and pushes an approval step.
criteria.reuse_crm_workflows: Reuse the existing dsr.crm_workflows criteria evaluator as the branch engine and only add the approval step and chain on top of it.

verdict.instructions: Do these two choices give WF-092 a correct and mergeable shape, given the measured evidence above?

criteria.accept: Both choices are right for this repository as measured.
criteria.revise: One of the two choices is wrong or incomplete.
criteria.reject: The shape is fundamentally wrong and needs rework.

decision: WF-092 blocking defect after naming the domain package

new_evidence_gathered.issue_157_what_to_build: The issue names backend/dsr/quote_approvals/ explicitly and lists it as a path the feature owns. No such package exists on main.
new_evidence_gathered.task_md_instruction: If a package for your domain ALREADY EXISTS under backend/dsr/, extend it. Do not create a second one for the same domain. The listed packages already on main are crm_integration, throttle, lead_score, visitor_identification, lead_qualification, round_robin, concierge_router. quote_approvals is NOT among them.
new_evidence_gathered.quoting_proposals_package_contents: rules.py vocabulary.py inferences.py engine.py plus quote_expiry_rules.py quote_expiry_vocabulary.py quote_expiry_engine.py quote_expiry_inferences.py. So the existing precedent inside that package is to add a suffixed module set for a second workflow in the same domain rather than a second package.
new_evidence_gathered.wf098_precedent: WF-098 quote expiry did exactly that. It added quote_expiry_*.py modules inside dsr/quoting_proposals/ and its own feature module, and did not create a new package.
new_evidence_gathered.wf091_coordination: The issue says WF-091 Route a discounted quote for standard approval covers the single level case and that both documents describe the same Settings > Objects > Quotes > Approvals tab, so there is a shared approval record shape to coordinate rather than diverge. WF-091 does not exist on main yet.

state.question_to_answer: The previous verdict was reject at confidence 0.46 with domain_package at 0.53. Which single defect caused the reject?

dominant_defect.instructions: Given the new evidence, what is the one thing wrong with creating backend/dsr/quote_approvals/ as the domain package for WF-092?

criteria.none_wrong: Nothing is wrong. The package location and shape are correct and the reject was driven by something outside the package decision.
criteria.should_extend_quoting_proposals: The domain rules belong in the existing dsr/quoting_proposals/ package, following the quote_expiry_* modules precedent, not in a new package.
criteria.needs_wf091_first: WF-091 must land first because the two features share one approval record shape, and building WF-092 alone would fork that shape.

verdict.instructions: After fixing the dominant defect, is WF-092 now ready to build and merge?

criteria.accept: The shape is right. Build it and merge.
criteria.revise: A specific further change is needed.

domain_rules_to_implement.branch_predicate: The researched HubSpot branch. Set Branch 1 to greater than 5,000 is the start of an advanced approval workflow for any quotes above 5,000. The room threshold is 5000 USD, chosen over the NetSuite 3000 example because the HubSpot example is the primary source of this ticket.
domain_rules_to_implement.limits: Up to five sequences and ten approvers per sequence. Enforced in validation and tested at the boundary.
domain_rules_to_implement.requirements: All approvers, Any approvers, Sequential. All three built.
domain_rules_to_implement.sequential_rule: Sequential approvals require approval by every approver at each priority step. A lower priority approver is not notified until every approver at the current priority has decided.
domain_rules_to_implement.auto_approval: If a quote approval step has not been added above this action, quotes will be auto-approved. A quote that matches a branch but has no approval step is approved, not blocked.
domain_rules_to_implement.final_state: The last decision writes APPROVED or REJECTED and the quote becomes publishable.
domain_rules_to_implement.single_workflow: You cannot duplicate the workflow or create a new workflow to use for quote approvals. One approval workflow record.
domain_rules_to_implement.message_template: The Message to approver field can embed quote properties via Choose data variable. The syntax derived and recorded is {{quote.property}} resolved against the quote record.
domain_rules_to_implement.re_enrolment: A toggle for quotes that need re-approval after edits. The state machine is not specified, so it is derived: re-enrolment resets the chain to the first priority and writes a new enrolment.
domain_rules_to_implement.notifications: Bell and email are built and stored as records. Teams, Slack and Google Chat are recorded as not built because the product has no confirmed delivery surface for them.
domain_rules_to_implement.wf091_coordination: WF-091 covers the single level case and does not exist on main. This build owns the shared approval record shape and names the collections so WF-091 can read them rather than fork them.

what_was_built.routes: 14 routes on prefix /api/wf-092, mounted by discovery with no shared file edited
what_was_built.frontend: frontend/src/features/wf-092-chain-sequential-multi-level-approvals-through-a-workflow/ with index.jsx, ApprovalChain.jsx, api.js, primitives.jsx, 18 vitest tests

researched_rules_enforced: Branch on one quote property with five operators. Default threshold 5000, greater_than, chosen from the HubSpot example over the NetSuite 3000 because the HubSpot figure is quoted as an approval branch. Recorded as DERIVED_THRESHOLD_IS_THE_HUBSPOT_FIGURE.
Cap of five sequences and ten approvers per sequence, enforced before any row is written and tested at the boundary.
Sequential approvals require approval by every approver at each priority step. A lower-priority decision is refused with outcome not_yet_your_priority and writes no row.
All approvers, Any approvers and Sequential, all three built and tested.
A quote with no approval step is auto-approved, not blocked. Tested.
The last decision writes APPROVED or REJECTED and the publishable flag together.
The approval workflow is single. A second one is refused with 409.
Notifications on bell and email, the two channels with a confirmed delivery surface. Teams, Slack and Google Chat are recorded as not built.
Re-enrolment resets the decisions and increments a run counter, derived and recorded.

design_decision.domain_package: Extended dsr/quoting_proposals rather than creating the dsr/quote_approvals package the issue names. Jev chose should_extend_quoting_proposals at confidence 0.97, with that option at 0.99, audit jev-20261005T064651-5128-11936. The package already holds a second workflow in the same domain as quote_expiry_*.py, and a team adding a quote field would otherwise have to know which package to edit.
